item: Just like you need ingredients to bake a cake, plants need special ingredients from nature to make their food. They collect water from soil and light from the sun. A garden flower absorbs rainwater through its roots and catches sunlight with its flat green leaves.

Inside the leaf, sunlight helps mix water and air together. This chemical reaction creates sugar, which is the main food that helps the plant grow big and strong. A tall oak tree uses this leaf sugar every day to build thick branches and fresh green acorns.

In summary, plants trap energy from sunlight to turn water and air into sweet sugar food. During this process, plants also release clean oxygen for us to breathe. Forests of trees constantly make food while filling our atmosphere with fresh air for humans and animals.
Where does a garden flower collect water from? -> From the soil
What part of a plant catches sunlight? -> Flat green leaves
What main food is created inside the leaf during photosynthesis? -> Sugar
How does a tall oak tree use the sugar made by its leaves? -> To build thick branches and fresh green acorns
What do plants release into the air while making their food? -> Clean oxygen

Newton's first law states that an object will stay still or keep moving at a steady speed unless an outside force pushes or pulls it. A soccer ball stays completely still on the grass until you kick it into the air.

Newton's second law shows that heavier objects need a larger force to accelerate, while lighter objects move much faster with the same amount of push. Pushing an empty shopping cart is very easy, but pushing a full cart requires much more strength.

Newton's laws explain how forces create motion, how mass affects movement speed, and how every single push creates an equal push in the opposite direction. Understanding these basic rules helps engineers design safer cars, fast airplanes, and incredible space rockets.
According to Newton's first law, what happens to an object unless an outside force acts on it? -> It will stay still or keep moving at a steady speed.
What example is used in the text to demonstrate Newton's first law? -> A soccer ball staying still on the grass until it is kicked
According to Newton's second law, what requires a larger force to accelerate? -> Heavier objects
Why is pushing a full shopping cart harder than pushing an empty one? -> Heavier objects require much more strength to push.
How does understanding Newton's laws help engineers? -> It helps them design safer cars, fast airplanes, and space rockets.
